sources.entry: SkilLock by skills-lock - Pin AI Skill behavior. Block unapproved drift in CI. See exactly what changed in every PR.

summary.one_liner: SkilLock is a Go CLI and GitHub Action that pins the literal capability surface (shell commands, network hosts, file paths, allowed tools, bundled scripts) of Claude Code and Codex Skills in a committed skills.lock file and blocks unapproved drift in pull requests.
summary.what_it_does: It scans .claude/skills/ and .codex/skills/ SKILL.md files and bundled scripts, extracting shell verbs, network URLs, file reads and writes, and allowed-tools written literally in the skill. A baseline is committed as skills.lock via "init --baseline", and the "ci" command re-scans and diffs capability sets rather than raw text. On each PR, a GitHub Action posts a comment listing added or removed capabilities with severity and reason, and returns BLOCK until a paste-ready approval entry is recorded in .skil-lock-approvals.yaml. It can also emit SARIF v2.1.0 for GitHub Code Scanning, and offers scan, lock, list, and diff subcommands. Per-file content digests bind approvals to the exact script body reviewed.
use_cases: gate AI skill changes in pull requests
review what a Claude Code skill can execute or reach
pin approved SKILL.md behavior in a repo
detect new curl or network calls added to agent skills
upload skill capability findings to GitHub Code Scanning
audit approvals of agent skill changes
how_to_run: go install github.com/skills-lock/skil-lock/cmd/skil-lock@v0.2.5  (or use prebuilt binary or Homebrew: brew install skills-lock/tap/skil-lock)
git add skills.lock && git commit -m "Pin approved AI Skill behavior"
Add .github/workflows/skil-lock.yml using uses: skills-lock/skil-lock-action@v0.2.1 with pin-binary: v0.2.5
skil-lock ci  (run locally to preview the PR comment)
skil-lock scan . / skil-lock list . / skil-lock diff old.lock new.lock for inspection
notable: Diffs capability sets (shell, URLs, paths, tools) instead of raw text, so prose edits do not create noise
Approvals are recorded in git with reviewer, timestamp, and reason, and PR-scoped approvals re-block reintroduced deltas
Hashes every file a skill ships and binds approvals to the reviewed digest
Explicit detection boundary: documents what is not caught, such as runtime-assembled commands and natural-language intent
Maps findings to OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 (AST01-AST10) IDs in SARIF output
caveats: Only Claude Code and Codex are supported in v0.1; Cursor, Copilot Skills, and Windsurf/MCP are planned
Static literal-text detection only: runtime-assembled commands, base64/eval-hidden URLs, natural-language intent, MCP servers, and cross-file references are not caught
Not a sandbox; the README states it does not analyze natural-language intent
keywords: security review for markdown agent instructions
